name: Boron

discovery.discoverer: Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac & Louis Jacques Thénard

occurrence: Found in borax and boric acid deposits, mostly from evaporated ancient lake beds.
majorUses: Neutron-absorbing control rods in nuclear reactors
biologicalRelevance: An essential trace nutrient for plants, needed for cell wall structure — its absence causes stunted, deformed growth.
notableCharacteristics: Only three valence electrons but forms famously electron-deficient compounds like diborane (B₂H₆) that break the usual bonding rules.
whyHere: With just three valence electrons in the p-block's first row, boron can't complete an octet through normal bonding alone — which is exactly why it forms unusual electron-deficient, three-centre-two-electron bonds.
didYouKnow: Boron is the reason Pyrex glassware can go from freezer to oven without shattering — borosilicate glass barely expands when heated.
genZNote: Three electrons short of a full house and somehow that's its whole personality. Chaotic bonding, glass-saving legacy.
